why: The spring that gives Greenspring its name rises here, beside the spring house.
This season's pit at the seep's south margin: the diggers cut down through the peat to the orange bog-iron layer and the seep fills the hole behind them.
A pit dug at the water's edge, reached by the duckboards; the cakes lie further out each season.
Last season's pit, worked out and left to flood beside the ore heaps.
The hatchery pool, cut into the toe of the bank under the tree so its root runs down into the water where the clutches are laid.
